rows.exemplarMemorable: the agent panel sliding in over the issue and starting to think
tells: A is the Linear homepage hero; B is a passage-planning product called Halyard
A sequences one thing at a time: headline blurs in 0.3 to 1.0s, subline at 1.2s, app window rises 1.3 to 1.9s, then the agent panel arrives about 3.5s and runs
A's climax is the product acting: the agent chat panel opens over the issue and starts 'Thinking'
B's card fades in late (0.96 to 1.5s) while the headline sits static, then nothing happens until the cursor presses Find windows near 5s; the clip ends on 'Checking' with no result
B's iridescent gradient behind the card is decorative and competes with the data

corrections.problem: the press lands in the last second, so the payoff (windows found) never appears in the moment
corrections.change: press at about 2.0s so the scan and the found windows land by 4.5s, then hold the result 1.5s
corrections.keep: the cursor travel into the button and the label changing to Checking in place

corrections.problem: 3.3s of a static card after its entrance with nothing owning the screen
corrections.change: cut the dead hold to about 1.2s, enough to read the route title and the four constraint chips

corrections.problem: card fades from near white with a soft blur, reading as loading rather than arriving
corrections.change: rise 8 to 12px with opacity over about 400ms on a decelerating curve, chips and chart offset about 80ms behind the header
corrections.keep: the headline already in place on the left

corrections.problem: the rainbow halo is decoration that pulls the eye off the tide chart
corrections.change: replace with a flat neutral surface or a single quiet tint

rows.memorable: the scan line sweeping the day and leaving two pink windows behind
rows.exemplarMemorable: the checkout re-localizing from $5.46 to EUR 26.89 row by row in place
tells: A is the Stripe homepage payments module; B is the Halyard planning card

A changes everything in place around 4.9 to 5.4s: the price, line items and checkout fields roll vertically from the US roastery to a German Cartsy checkout with a staggered offset of roughly a tenth of a second per row
A holds each state about 5s, long enough to read the price and line items aloud
B does tell a full product story (press at 3.3s, scan sweep 4.5 to 6.5s, wind bars turn amber, two windows and a proposed plan by 7.5 to 8s) and holds the result 4s
B's scan lasts about 3s, a loading state the viewer just waits through; the plan panel breaks out past the card edge and the card itself rescales between 0.0 and 0.1s

corrections.where: B 4.5 to 7.5s, scan line and 'Checking 05:00 to 20:00'
corrections.problem: about 3s of sweeping before any answer appears, so the product's result arrives late and the sweep reads as decoration
corrections.change: run the sweep in about 1.2s and drop each window into its row the moment the line passes it
corrections.keep: the wind bars turning amber as the line crosses the over-limit hours

corrections.problem: it slides up overlapping and overhanging the card's bottom edge and right edge, so two surfaces fight for ownership
corrections.change: seat the plan inside the card below the Back row, or give it a clear gap and align its right edge to the card
corrections.keep: the four large times and the 'Daylight to spare 3 h 46 min' figure

corrections.problem: the card jumps in scale and position at the start of the clip
corrections.change: start the card at its final size and position
corrections.keep: the two-second calm hold before the cursor moves

corrections.problem: '2 windows found' replaces 'Checking' in small type at the top right while the eye is on the chart
corrections.change: let the found windows themselves carry the news first, then update the header about 100ms later

rows.memorable: the forecast badge flipping from Fri 18:00 to Fri 21:00
rows.exemplarMemorable: the checkout re-localizing row by row in place
tells: B is the same Stripe payments module, rolling the whole checkout to a new locale in place at about 5s
A (Halyard) updates the forecast badge, window end time and first warning time with in-place vertical rolls at 3.4 to 3.8s, which is good
A's notification still reads 'back 11:10 to 13:45' for about 3s after the card already says 13:20, so the screen contradicts itself
A's key change is tiny: the pink window shrinks a few pixels for 25 minutes, so the moment that matters is the least visible
A opens with a cut from the hero to blank white and a fade (0.0 to 0.4s)

corrections.problem: the old notification still says 13:45 while the card above says 13:20, so the information on screen is wrong for 3s
corrections.change: bring the 'Back window moved' notification in within about 0.3s of the card update, or update the card after the notification arrives
corrections.keep: the notification copy 'Now closes 13:20, 25 minutes earlier'

corrections.problem: the window's right edge pulls in a few pixels and is easy to miss
corrections.change: flash the lost 25 minutes as a hatched sliver that fades over about 600ms so the loss is visible
corrections.keep: the window staying in place on the timeline

corrections.problem: the new notification pushes in under the old one so two cards overlap for a moment
corrections.change: cross-swap the notification contents in place, or slide the old one out before the new one lands

corrections.problem: hard cut from the hero to a white frame, then a fade
corrections.change: start on the settled card, or move into it with a continuous scroll
corrections.keep: the two-second calm hold before the forecast changes

rows.memorable: the dot stepping through the Solent with the clock advancing
rows.exemplarMemorable: the checkout re-localizing row by row in place
tells: B is again the Stripe payments module with its in-place locale swap
A (Halyard) moves a boat dot through Jack in the Basket, Hamstead Ledge, Gurnard and Cowes, about 1.5s per leg, with the readout updating after each arrival
In A the solid track is drawn after the dot arrives (dot reaches the waypoint at 7.0s, line fills 7.2 to 7.4s), so the trail lags its own cause
In A every leg takes about the same time although the legs span 18, 29, 42 and 11 minutes, so screen time does not match passage time
In A the Stream field reads 'With you' for the whole passage and never earns its place; the readout numbers jump rather than count

corrections.where: A 6.6 to 7.4s, Hamstead Ledge to Gurnard leg
corrections.problem: the dot travels first and the solid line is drawn behind it about 0.3s later
corrections.change: draw the solid track with the dot as its leading tip on the same curve and duration
corrections.keep: the dashed future route ahead of the dot

corrections.problem: each leg gets the same screen time regardless of how long it takes on the water
corrections.change: scale each leg's duration to its minutes (11 min leg shortest, 42 min leg longest) with a short ease in and out at each waypoint
corrections.keep: the brief pause at each named waypoint

corrections.problem: time and distance roll to the new value only after the dot stops, and jump rather than track progress
corrections.change: count time and distance up continuously as the dot moves, and roll the place name in at arrival
corrections.keep: the three-column readout and its type sizes

corrections.problem: blank cream frame and fade before the map appears
corrections.keep: the 1.5s hold at Lymington before departure

corrections.problem: 'With you' never changes, so it is dead information on screen
corrections.change: change it when the stream turns, or replace it with a value that moves, such as speed over ground
